title: OpenWeights supply-chain scan, convert, certify, and safeguard pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a unified end-to-end pipeline that ingests community/open-source model weights and produces a production-ready, pinned runtime artifact with safety and provenance guarantees. This ticket covers: scanning the weight bundle for provenance and license signals, static and dynamic integrity checks, deterministic conversion into the runtime format (including graph/shape normalization and favorite quantization candidates), automated smoke and regression validation, a lightweight human review gating step for flagged artifacts, and publishing a performance profile + recommended pin with metadata for the Console and model catalog. The pipeline must be auditable, idempotent, and support fast rollback of an automatically suggested pin. Store intermediate artifacts in ephemeral secure storage (S3 with KMS) and emit structured telemetry to the Console. Avoid duplicating existing intake components; integrate with Artifact Gateway team hooks and existing profiling runners where possible.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline accepts a tar.gz weight bundle and returns a deterministic runtime artifact with a stable tag
License and provenance scanner runs and emits structured flags to the audit log
Conversion step produces at least one quantization candidate and records expected throughput/latency profiles
Automated smoke tests (sample prompts + deterministic output checks) pass in CI-staging
Console model catalog receives profile metadata and suggested pin with SLO estimates
Human-in-loop review flow can block publish if license/safety flags exist
Telemetry includes token-level latency histogram, peak mem usage, and batch-scaling curves
Rollback path allows pin replacement and will automatically route traffic to fallback variants
implementation_notes: Design choices: (1) Run a fast static checksum + manifest validator first to reject corrupt archives; (2) Perform a signature and license scan (spdx heuristics) to classify artifacts; (3) Convert to runtime format using deterministic seed and reproducible build env (containerized build image with pinned toolchain); (4) Generate 2 quantization candidates (INT8 and dynamic FP16) and run profiling harness for each at 4 sequence lengths; (5) Run KV-cache and prefix-caching smoke tests to detect cache-compat regressions; (6) Emit a draft performance profile and delta vs nearest existing model to aid pin recommendation. Trade-offs: adding more quantization candidates increases CI time; we keep baseline to 2 to balance coverage and cycle time. Integration: call /artifact-gateway/validate webhook and push profile to /catalog/publish API. Security: write intermediate artifacts encrypted and restrict decryption to build role only.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Malicious or malformed weights may attempt side-channel or code-execute during conversion. Mitigation: run conversion in hardened sandbox (seccomp) with network disabled and ephemeral IAM credentials
Risk: License ambiguity slowing human review. Mitigation: add automated license-similarity scoring and escalate only high-ambiguity cases to legal
Risk: Performance regressions post-pin. Mitigation: require canary rollout to traffic-limited Dedicated pool with automatic rollback on latency or error anomaly
runbook_summary: If pipeline fails at conversion: capture build logs and artifact checksum, mark ingress as quarantined, kick a retry with increased memory. If smoke tests fail: mark candidate as failed and surface failure diff in Console; block publish. If telemetry shows 2x latency on canary: auto-fail and replace pin with last-known-good variant and alert on-call infra.
